messages.subject: Missing p values
parts:
Hello MSstats team,

I am analyzing a data set consisting of 2 groups, 3 replicates each. First, I am imputing the missing values and then performing groups comparison. 
I noticed that in some cases the p-value is missing from the group comparison lines, specifically, when the ratio between the replicates that the protein was found in is 1:3 or 1:2 (In other words, when in group A the protein was found in 1 replicate from 3, and in group B in 2 replicates from 3). I am not sure if it has something to do with the imputation limit because the log2FC is present, but maybe im wrong. 
If not, is there something wrong with my code or how can I overcome this problem? 
I am attaching the r code I am using, and part of the output (The missing p-value lines I am talking about are 16, 17, 45, 48, 68, 84, 89, 94.)

Thank you in advance for all your help!

analyzed_data <- dataSummarizationPTM(
  raw,
  logTrans = 2,
  normalization = FALSE,
  normalization.PTM = FALSE,
  nameStandards = NULL,
  nameStandards.PTM = NULL,
  featureSubset = "all",
  featureSubset.PTM = "all",
  remove_uninformative_feature_outlier = FALSE,
  remove_uninformative_feature_outlier.PTM = FALSE,
  n_top_feature = "all",
  n_top_feature.PTM = "all",
  summaryMethod = "TMP",
  equalFeatureVar = TRUE,
  censoredInt = "NA",
  MBimpute = TRUE,
  MBimpute.PTM = TRUE,
  remove50missing = FALSE,
  fix_missing = NULL,
  use_log_file = TRUE,
  append = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE,
  log_file_path = NULL,
  base = "MSstatsPTM_log_"
  )


comarison_results <- groupComparisonPTM(
  analyzed_data,
  data.type =  "LabelFree",
  contrast.matrix = "pairwise",
  log_base = 2,
  use_log_file = TRUE,
  append = FALSE,
  verbose = TRUE,
  log_file_path = NULL,
  base = "MSstatsPTM_log_"
)

messages.author: 13904eb0f06097b0
messages.subject: Re: Missing p values
parts:
Hi Lara,

Ok that makes sense. Did you generate the `msstats.csv` file from FragPipe? It's actually really easy to use MSstatsPTM with FragPipe via the converter. I've included some code below to get the workflow started. From there you can just use the code you sent over.

One note is that without a global profiling run we generally do not recommend normalizing for changes in the underlying protein level. We can extract unmodified peptides from the enriched run and use them in place of the global profiling run, however this usually does not work as well.

```
fragpipe_input = read.csv("msstats.csv")

msstats_data = FragPipetoMSstatsPTMFormat(fragpipe_input,
                                          label_type="LF",
                                          mod_id_col = "STY", # Just add in the name of the modification column in the msstats.csv file
                                          use_unmod_peptides=FALSE # Set this to TRUE if you want to extract unmod peptides for normalization
)
```

Devon

Hi Lara,

Apologies I forgot that the id columns for label free are different than TMT. This converter actually works for both label free and TMT now, the documentation needs to be updated on our end.

So you actually do need to use the converter because it will format the data into MSstatsPTM format. The FragPipe output just gives you the information needed for the formatting.

Can you try the updated code below? It runs for the example FragPipe data I have.

```
fragpipe_input = read.csv("msstats.csv")

msstats_data = FragPipetoMSstatsPTMFormat(fragpipe_input, 
                                    label_type="LF",

protein_id_col="ProteinName", 
                                    peptide_id_col = "PeptideSequence")
```

Devon
